output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson) – Aria 3 recalibration

I promised Dana I would write this up after my writer had been through a real trial. It has now had eight days of a civil trial, and I can give Harbor Point a recommendation, with one important reservation about reaching them by phone.

I dropped off my Stenvale Aria 3 on Monday, October 19, for a full recalibration, a number bar sensor inspection, cleaning and a firmware update. Harbor Point quoted $285 and an estimated 10 business days. I picked it up Tuesday, October 27, six business days later.

The final invoice was $310: the original $285 for parts and labor, plus $25 to replace the internal battery. Gloria Ruark emailed to say the battery was holding about 60% of its rated capacity and asked before adding the replacement. I approved it. That matters to me, and I think $310 was fair for what was done. I paid for it myself, as I do all my equipment; the court did not reimburse me. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

According to the invoice, Gloria recalibrated the keyboard, replaced the number bar depression sensor, cleaned the machine internally, updated the firmware and replaced the battery. The machine also came back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I have never had that from anyone before, and I appreciated having something clear to keep with my records.

The first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. It has since made it through eight days of trial, and that is enough real work for me to feel comfortable reporting on it.

Harbor Point offered me an Aria 2 loaner. It kept me working, but its tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, and I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I told Gloria, and she said they would repair the arm before sending it out again.

My reservation is the phone. I called Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress. It rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed the following day. Their phone is staffed only Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4, which is a real weakness if you are working a Monday docket and need to reach someone. I would not count on getting a quick answer by phone outside those hours.

The shop is a two-person operation off York Road, with free parking in back. Dana, based on my experience, I would trust Gloria with your Aria 3, especially for the number bar problem. I would also make a plan for the time without it, check the loaner’s tilt arm before you leave, and go in knowing the limits of their phone availability. The work on my machine was good; the difficulty reaching the shop is worth weighing alongside it.

Maureen
